patterns: Java ELEMENT_QUERY (java.rs): literal text is '(method_declaration name: (identifier) @method_name) @function' plus '(class_declaration name: (identifier) @class_name) @class', '(interface_declaration name: (identifier) @interface_name) @class', '(enum_declaration name: (identifier) @enum_name) @class'.

parser_elements.rs matches capture names 'func_name' | 'method_name' for function names and 'class_name' | 'type_name' for class names; if absent it falls back to child_by_field_name('name').

constraints: Maintainer note in #1864: the maintainers implement this in-house and external pull requests are not accepted. This Scout output is research only.

Crate must clear the 7-day package age gate (check-package-age.sh) without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK. Latest tree-sitter-php tag v0.25.2 was released 2026-11-19 (about 8 to 9 days before the run). The crates.io created_at timestamp was not verified (no crates.io access).
tree-sitter-php dev-dependency is tree-sitter 0.27 and depends on tree-sitter-language 0.1; the lock has tree-sitter 0.27.2 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.9, so these are compatible.
Workspace tree-sitter is declared 0.27.1 while mod.rs comments refer to a tree-sitter 0.26 API; the lock is 0.27.2. Treat the comment as stale.
rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.100.0 while Cargo.toml rust-version is 1.98.0; both must be satisfied by new code.
Scope per #1864: no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no property or constant extraction; no trait use resolution; no namespace import aliasing; no tool handler or schema changes.

DEFUSE_QUERY is required for the defuse path: parser.rs compiles lang_info.defuse_query when Some and parser_elements.rs extract_def_use returns no sites when it is None. The Java and Swift handlers both set it.
queries are compiled lazily per language via QUERY_CACHE keyed on supported_languages(); php must appear there or its queries cannot be loaded.
EXTENSION_MAP drives the schema pattern (schema_helpers::supported_file_ext_pattern) and must stay ECMAScript-valid; adding ('php', 'php') needs no regex change.
css is wired in get_language_info and get_ts_language and EXTENSION_MAP but is absent from supported_languages(); this is an existing inconsistency, not something to copy.
test_coverage: Inline unit tests exist for java.rs (element query, inheritance, defuse write site, receiver functions), swift.rs (queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element query, inheritance) and css.rs (element, import, empty-file). lang.rs tests cover extension lookup happy and edge paths and the schema pattern; mod.rs tests cover known and unknown languages and a table-driven check of reference and import presence. Core integration tests cover java, csharp, javascript, fortran inheritance and parse. No existing test covers php, and there is no .php fixture.

approaches.name: A. Full registry mirror of Swift/Java (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to the workspace and core Cargo.toml; create languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY (free, member and scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name based), and extract_inheritance covering class, interface and enum; wire 'php' into EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages(), get_language_info() and get_ts_language(); add unit tests in php.rs, an integration test under crates/aptu-coder/tests/, and README updates.
pros: Matches the issue's five-query contract and the Swift/Java pattern exactly.
Confined to core crate plus one new test file; no tool handler or schema changes.
LANGUAGE_PHP handles mixed HTML and PHP through the grammar's text and php_tag nodes.
cons: Depends on the 7-day age gate for the 2026-11-19 release (crates.io timestamp unverified).
Import handling uses the generic full-text fallback, so the module string is the whole 'use ...;' statement rather than split items.

approaches.name: B. Minimal element-only integration
approaches.description: Same dependency and registry wiring, but omit CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY (set them to None or empty) and implement only ELEMENT_QUERY and extract_inheritance.
pros: Smallest diff and quickest path through the age gate and review.
cons: Does not meet the issue's acceptance criteria for calls, imports and defuse.
Calls in analyze_file would be empty, failing the '->' and '::' acceptance criterion.

approaches.name: C. Two grammar entry points (LANGUAGE_PHP and LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY)
approaches.description: Register 'php' with LANGUAGE_PHP for .php files; optionally add a second name (for example 'php_only') using LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for pure-PHP sources, sharing the same query constants.
pros: Pure-PHP files parse without HTML text nodes, which may simplify queries.
Exposes the grammar's second entry point, which the issue leaves to the implementer.
cons: Adds a language key that the issue does not ask for and that the schema and README would have to document.
Two entry points double the query-compile tests with no acceptance benefit.

recommendation: Approach A. It meets every acceptance criterion in #1864, follows the Java and Swift registry pattern, and uses LANGUAGE_PHP so that the HTML-template criterion is handled by the grammar's text node. Approach B fails the call and defuse criteria. Approach C is out of scope. Before implementation, confirm the tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 crates.io created_at is at least 7 days old, and note that the generic import fallback stores the whole use statement as the module string.

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: tree-sitter-php common/define-grammar.js (fetched via gh api, master, matches v0.25.2). class_declaration = seq(optional(field attributes), repeat(_modifier), keyword class, field name (name), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field body (declaration_list)). Walk: (1) from the class_declaration node, iterate node.children (not child_by_field_name, because base_clause and class_interface_clause are unfielded). (2) For each child whose kind is base_clause, iterate its named children; base_clause = seq(keyword extends, commaSep1(_name)), so each named child is name, qualified_name or relative_name; emit 'extends <text>' for each. (3) For each child whose kind is class_interface_clause, iterate its named children; class_interface_clause = seq(keyword implements, commaSep1(_name)); emit 'implements <text>' for each. (4) Keyword tokens are anonymous and skipped by named_child iteration. Interface_declaration also carries base_clause for its extends list, so the same walk emits 'extends' for interfaces. enum_declaration carries class_interface_clause for implements and may carry a primitive_type child for its backing type, which the walk must ignore. Text for qualified_name keeps any leading backslash; strip it if the contract needs bare names.
